 This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court

 Order
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 12.09.2018 passed in MACC No.74/2018 by M.A.C.T, Rewa District-Rewa seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that from medical evidence on record, it is clearly established that appellant suffered 40% permanent disability but Tribunal has wrongly held that appellant did not suffer any permanent disability.
No amount has been awarded for loss of future earning capacity.
At the time of accident, appellant was a practicing Advocate.

Therefore, 40%
should have been added as future prospects.
It is also urged that no amount has been awarded for loss of amenities.
Further, only Rs.5,000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering.

With respect to above, learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon T. P. Parameshwarappa @
Parameshwarappa Vs. The Branch Manager New India Assurance Co. Ltd, & Ors 2022 SCC Online SC 1604.

sentences.text: Therefore, on above grounds, it is urged that compensation awarded by Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just & proper.
No enhancement is required.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

6. So far as permanent disability is concerned, perusal of para-24 and 25 of impugned award reveal that Tribunal has held that there is contradiction in the statements of applicant witness Dr. L.D.
Jatav and Dr. Hemant Bhandari with respect to disability as well as loss of functionality.

Therefore,
Tribunal held that it is not established that appellant suffered any sort of permanent disability on account of injuries sustained in the accident.

sentences.text: Perusal of depositions of applicant witness Dr. Hemant Bhandari and Dr. L.D. Jatav reveal that only contradiction in their deposition is with respect to the aspect of functional disability and not physical disability.
As per Dr. Hemant Bhandari, there was problem in appellant's right knee and there is 20 degree less movement in right knee.
Dr. L.D. Jatav has also specifically mentioned that there was stiffness in appellant's knee and he was unable to sit on ground.

Further, it is correct that applicant witness Satyendra Sharma has admitted in para-7 of cross-examination that he has come to the Court without any help of any instrument or stretcher but this witness has deposed in para-9 of his cross- examination that he cannot walk for long distance at one stretch and if he continue to stand for longer time, then, there is swelling etc. in the leg.
Dr. L.D. Jatav has also deposed in his cross-examination that injured cannot stand for long time and he cannot work for long stretch etc.
8. Admittedly, appellant is a practicing Lawyer in District Court and a Lawyer practicing in District Court, has to move frequently from his place of sitting to various Courts.
He cannot practice by sitting at one place.
Further, for arguments and examining a witness etc. a lawyer has to stand continuously for long duration.

As per Dr. L.D. Jatav and permanent disability certificate (
Ex.P/170), permanent disability assessed by Medical Board is 40% but it is with reference to particular part of body and not in relation to whole of the body.
9. Therefore, in this Court's opinion, Tribunal has erred in concluding that appellant did not suffer any kind of permanent disability (both physical as well as functional disability).

Hence, in view of overall facts and circumstances of the case, permanent physical as well as functional disability is assessed as 10%.
10.
In the instant case, Tribunal has determined appellant's monthly income as Rs.10,000/- per month.
At the time of accident, appellant was aged about 34 years.
Therefore, 40% is to be added as future prospects and in view of age of appellant, multiplier of 16 is to be applied.
Further, Tribunal has not awarded any amount for loss of amenities.
Tribunal has awarded only Rs.5,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.20,000/- for special diet.

11. Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
 S.No. Heads C  1. Monthly Income of the appellant R  2.
Additional Future prospect 40% R 3.

Annual Income of appellant (monthly income, Rs.14,000/- x 12 including future prospects x12)
4.

Annual Income of appellant Rs.1,68,000/-
5. Loss of Future Earnings Per annum (10% of Rs.16,800/-
Permanent Functional Disability )

6. Total loss of future earnings (Loss of future Rs.2,68,800/-

13. Enhanced compensation Rs.3,93,800/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
